device_scope: all Radeon devices sharing one loaded module
source_relation: radeon_gart_size is one writable module-global integer initialized to minus one. The first device argument check replaces auto or invalid input in that shared integer with its family default, then copies the latched value into the device memory-controller state.
lock_or_order: Module insertion establishes the request before PCI probe. Each device argument check may mutate the shared request before publishing mc.gtt_size for that device.
failure_contract: A later module-parameter write changes the shared request but does not rerun address placement, metadata allocation, TTM initialization, or register programming for an initialized device.
measurement_surface: module load command;PCI probe order;kernel GTT log;module parameter value
optimization_effect: Requires an explicit module-load gartsize value for comparable trials and records probe order as a confounder.
nonclaim: The parameter value read after initialization does not prove the value programmed for an existing device.

source_relation: An explicit gartsize of at least 32 MiB and a power of two reaches mc.gtt_size. Auto, a value below 32 MiB, or a non-power-of-two value becomes the first probed family default. Every family below CHIP_RV770 resolves that default to 512 MiB, so the latched value does not identify RS482 as the first probed device.
lock_or_order: Argument validation completes before mc.gtt_size is published and before ASIC selection.
failure_contract: Invalid explicit values warn and become the first probed family default rather than reaching RS400 programming as written.
measurement_surface: module load command;kernel warning;per-device GTT log
optimization_effect: Defines the requested aperture input but cannot select a workload optimum.
nonclaim: A source-accepted or default size is not a target allocation, stability, or performance verdict.

source_relation: RS400 accepts 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, and 2048 MiB and maps each to one RS480_VA_SIZE code before setting RS480_GART_EN.
lock_or_order: Selector normalization precedes memory-controller placement, page allocation, and hardware programming.
failure_contract: An unsupported size is forced to 32 MiB by rs400_gart_adjust_size; a later unrecognized effective size returns EINVAL from GART initialization or enable.
optimization_effect: Proves the requested candidate encodings exist without preferring one.
nonclaim: A register encoding does not prove that the aperture is usable under pressure.

source_relation: RS400 sets gtt_base_align to the normalized power-of-two size minus one. radeon_gtt_location aligns the regions before and after VRAM to that size and selects the larger region. A valid selector therefore remains nominal or collapses to zero before later selector admission.
lock_or_order: VRAM location and the nominal alignment mask are established before GTT placement; the inclusive GTT interval is published before GART allocation.
failure_contract: A zero effective size reaches rs400_gart_init and returns EINVAL. The source does not silently program an arbitrary intermediate size for an admitted selector.
measurement_surface: kernel log;retained GTT interval;requested and effective size
optimization_effect: Separates module input, normalized selector, address-fit result, and programmed aperture into distinct evidence fields.
nonclaim: The source derivation does not prove either candidate region or a successful target boot.

source_relation: CPU and GPU page counts equal effective gtt_size divided by their page sizes. Linux allocates one pointer per CPU page, one u64 shadow per GPU page, and RS400 allocates one four-byte hardware PTE per GPU page.
lock_or_order: Page counts precede both shadow allocations, RS400 table sizing, and coherent table allocation.
failure_contract: Each common shadow allocation failure calls radeon_gart_fini for its completed ownership prefix. A hardware table allocation failure returns ENOMEM and the outer RS400 init aborts.
optimization_effect: Quantifies fixed modeled metadata cost for each effective aperture before payload pages are committed.
nonclaim: The model excludes the dummy page, allocator metadata, host page tables, and payload backing.

source_relation: Linux derives GPU-usable VRAM from the northbridge TOM interval and exposes that fixed firmware-visible interval to the VRAM manager.
lock_or_order: Northbridge TOM and aperture discovery precede VRAM manager initialization.
failure_contract: Invalid or constrained aperture state can limit driver-visible VRAM, but Linux does not return firmware-reserved DRAM to the operating system.
optimization_effect: Keeps the physical VRAM pool distinct from the GTT virtual aperture.
nonclaim: The source relation does not prove that every boot reserves 128 MiB.

source_relation: vramlimit can reduce real_vram_size after the physical VRAM interval is established, and its module description marks the control as testing-only.
lock_or_order: The limit changes driver accounting after vram_start and vram_end derive from the firmware-visible interval.
failure_contract: Zero or a non-power-of-two value leaves the physical interval unchanged and disables the limit.
optimization_effect: Shows that lowering the driver limit cannot reclaim the firmware carveout and therefore is not a memory optimization.
nonclaim: A smaller reported VRAM size does not increase system RAM or GTT bandwidth.

source_relation: TTM initializes the VRAM range-manager maximum from real_vram_size, sets its active size to visible_vram_size, pins the stolen VGA object, and initializes the GTT range manager from effective gtt_size.
lock_or_order: The VRAM maximum and active bound initialize before the stolen object; the GTT manager initializes afterward and before ordinary BO validation.
failure_contract: Each manager reports allocation failure, but later initialization failures return directly; the bounded source does not prove complete rollback of earlier TTM ownership.
optimization_effect: Defines allocator address capacity for both domains while preserving visible versus total VRAM.
nonclaim: GTT manager capacity is virtual aperture space, not uniquely available physical DRAM.

source_relation: For a multi-domain request Linux appends VRAM, then GTT, then CPU placement; CPU access constrains VRAM to the visible interval. A GTT placement at or below the 512 KiB segregation boundary requests top-of-aperture insertion (TTM_PL_FLAG_TOPDOWN), so small objects pack against the top of the aperture while wider requests cut from the bottom.
lock_or_order: Placement construction precedes each TTM validation attempt.
failure_contract: An empty domain request falls back to system placement.
optimization_effect: Makes requested domains and realized placement separate evidence fields, and keeps the middle of the aperture wide by segregating small GTT objects to the top.
nonclaim: Preferred order does not prove final placement, residency duration, or lower latency, and the 512 KiB segregation boundary is a heuristic, not a measured optimum.

source_relation: The per-IB threshold is max of one MiB and half the free portion of the lower half of real VRAM. For 128 MiB VRAM the intercept is 32 MiB, each two-byte usage increment lowers the raw threshold by one byte, and odd usage rounds down one additional byte. The byte-domain floor begins at 65,011,711 bytes; the first 4 KiB-aligned value at the floor is 62 MiB.
lock_or_order: The threshold snapshot precedes BO validation; the prior moved-byte total is compared with a strict greater-than test before each next preferred move.
failure_contract: A preferred-domain validation failure retries with allowed domains unless interrupted. A whole BO can overshoot the threshold because its size is counted only after validation.
optimization_effect: Defines the anti-thrash coefficients and the BO-size confounder that every workload comparison retains.
nonclaim: The source threshold and comment are not a measured optimum for RS482.

source_relation: The maximum single BO size is effective gtt_size minus gart_pin_size because VRAM-to-system migration uses the GTT path, including a BO initially requested in VRAM.
lock_or_order: The ceiling is checked before BO creation and before VRAM-to-GTT retry.
failure_contract: An oversized request returns ENOMEM without allocating a BO.
optimization_effect: Shows that effective GTT capacity and pinned debit constrain every single BO domain.
nonclaim: A larger single-BO ceiling does not prove physical backing, allocator extent, or successful placement.

source_relation: Linux tracks pinned bytes by realized VRAM or GTT placement and subtracts the counters from GEM_INFO visible VRAM and GTT capacity.
lock_or_order: Pin counters change only after successful placement and unwind on unpin.
failure_contract: Failed placement does not publish a pin count.
optimization_effect: Separates nominal capacity from capacity reserved by non-evictable objects.
nonclaim: Unpinned capacity is not the same as the largest allocatable extent.

source_relation: GEM_INFO reports active VRAM-manager size, visible VRAM minus pinned VRAM, and effective GTT minus pinned GTT. RADEON_INFO reports current VRAM usage, GTT usage, and cumulative bytes moved.
lock_or_order: The ioctl table binds both query functions; each query samples manager and movement state without submitting work.
failure_contract: A failed ioctl yields no observation and cannot be replaced by a zero value.
optimization_effect: Provides the minimum counter set for allocation-pressure and movement comparisons.
nonclaim: GEM_INFO does not by itself prove the firmware physical carveout, fragmentation, or end-to-end performance.

source_relation: Linux assigns each successfully created BO a per-device monotonic debug identity. GEM_BUSY traces bind the querying PID and handle to that identity, size, initial domain, realized domain, and result. radeon_gem_info reports the same identity with each tracked BO size and realized placement, while radeon_vram_mm and radeon_gtt_mm expose allocator extents.
lock_or_order: GEM initializes the identity counter before BO creation. A successful BO initialization assigns the identity before the creation trace. GEM_BUSY emits its trace before releasing the handle lookup reference. The debugfs BO list is read under gem.mutex.
failure_contract: A failed handle lookup emits no BO trace. Missing debugfs, tracefs, trace enablement, or permission denies the join and must not be treated as an empty allocator.
optimization_effect: Provides an event-scoped handle-to-BO-to-placement join and allocator extents needed to distinguish capacity exhaustion, migration, and fragmentation.
nonclaim: A debugfs snapshot does not prove placement stability across a concurrent allocator change, and a debug identity does not expose a GEM handle through UAPI.

device_scope: RS482 1002:5974 with a separately measured VRAM interval
source_relation: Linux source defines mechanisms, coefficients, and observation surfaces but cannot choose the optimal GTT aperture for the target.
lock_or_order: A fresh no-submit allocation-pressure baseline precedes reboot-gated explicit module-load trials; submit workloads run only after exact identity and recovery gates.
failure_contract: No candidate closes without retained requested and effective size, interval, allocation success, largest extent, placement, movement, BO-size distribution, workload, stability, and confounder evidence.
optimization_effect: Ranks 128, 256, 512, and 1024 MiB by a feasibility gate followed by measured headroom, extent, movement, copy count, latency, metadata, and stability.
nonclaim: The smallest aperture wins only when measured outcomes are equivalent; the largest aperture or highest fill ratio is not automatically optimal.
